question: Refer to the exhibit. A network engineer must configure an authentication solution for Cisco UCS with these conditions: two-factor authentication must be enabled for all UCS user authentication; and all AAA packets must be encrypted and use TCP port 49 to establish communication. Which set of actions meets these requirements?

theory: TACACS+ (unlike RADIUS) uses TCP port 49 and encrypts the entire AAA payload rather than just the password, matching the requirement for encrypted, TCP/49-based AAA traffic. Cisco UCS two-factor authentication is supported only when RADIUS or TACACS+ provider groups are associated with an authentication domain - it is not supported for LDAP, local, or none - so the existing LDAP provider must be removed and replaced with a TACACS+ provider to satisfy both the encryption and two-factor requirements together. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 19 - Two-Factor Authentication, RADIUS/TACACS+ AAA)
